If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to reflect overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast volatility by 15–25% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overfitting to recent sentiment noise.  
When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast for early horizon to capture momentum.  
When sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast for mid horizon to avoid false rebounds.  
If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.33) across 10+ days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast for late horizon to account for structural bearishness.
